title: Stamping tubes (bamboo)
summary: A set of bamboo tubes of different lengths, each cut open at the top and closed at the foot by a natural joint. Struck on the mouth with a pad of husk, or stamped on the ground, each tube sounds one hollow note, the long ones deep and the short ones high, and the players share a tune between them.
howToPlay: The tubes stand in a row on the sand: the longest and deepest at the left, the shortest and highest at the right.
Each lit tube gives its own note, and the notes rise from the longest tube to the shortest.
A ring closes on the mouth of the tube to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the long tubes, then work up to the short ones.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: Bamboo grows along the shores of the Pacific, and groups of players learned to cut tubes to length and share out a tune one note each. Each player cares for a single tube, so the music depends on the whole group listening to one another.
credits: Tradition: the Bamboo tubes; patterns written for this game
